displayContract.byline: Assessments made by 5.6 Sol. — Rubric: Slugfester Reassessment Rubric v2.

thesis.text: The strongest consciousness-first position treats experience as indispensable evidence and proposes a physics-preserving intrinsic realization theory whose merit depends on comparative explanatory integration, not novel dynamical predictions.

novelty.explanation: This steelman preserves the transcript's central route while answering the objection that unchanged physics necessarily means no explanatory contribution.

premises.text: Immediate conscious awareness is evidence with distinctive first-person access, and an adequate ontology must preserve its qualitative character rather than merely catalogue associated reports or neural transitions.

novelty.explanation: This develops the transcript's private-data requirement into a more explicit preservation condition for adequate explanation.

premises.text: Physical theory's equations characterize dynamical and relational organization extremely successfully while leaving open, at least conceptually, what intrinsic reality realizes that organization.

novelty.explanation: This combines respect for empirical constraints with the structural opening used by the Russellian proposal.

premises.text: A consciousness-first realizer can preserve every tested prediction and still contribute metaphysical explanation if it identifies what concretely instantiates physical structure and why qualitative reality belongs within nature.

novelty.explanation: This directly repairs the gap between unchanged dynamics and the claimed explanatory contribution of conscious realization.

premises.text: The proposal should be assessed comparatively against physicalism by explicit criteria including ontological economy, qualitative coverage, structural reconstruction, causal constitution, and compatibility with established science.

novelty.explanation: This supplies comparative criteria that empirical underdetermination alone did not establish in the live exchange.

premises.text: No completed consciousness-first theory is available unless it supplies principled composition rules explaining when simple conscious realizers form one subject and when they remain merely coordinated plurality.

novelty.explanation: This converts the conceded combination problem into an explicit completion condition rather than containing it rhetorically.

conclusion.text: Consciousness-first metaphysics therefore remains a serious explanatory research program if it can specify realization and composition while preserving physics; its present case supports comparative promise, not completed theoretical victory.

novelty.explanation: The conclusion proportionately limits the transcript's unification ambition by incorporating its strongest unresolved empirical and compositional burdens.

newArguments.title: Constraint-satisfaction comparison
newArguments.text: Treat the metaphysical contest as a constraint-satisfaction problem rather than a demand for novel particle predictions. Candidate ontologies must simultaneously preserve tested dynamics, accommodate first-person qualitative evidence, specify the realizers of physical structure, explain conscious unity, and avoid duplicating causal work. A consciousness-first theory gains support only if one coherent set of realization and composition principles satisfies more of these constraints with fewer independent primitives than its physicalist competitor. This framework makes explanatory improvement assessable even when both theories predict the same observations.

novelty.explanation: This introduces a new explicit model-selection framework that evaluates prediction-equivalent ontologies through jointly stated theoretical constraints.

newArguments.title: Constitutive intervention test
newArguments.text: Causal relevance need not require an additional force if consciousness constitutes the concrete realizer of physical dynamics. The proposal can nevertheless be disciplined counterfactually: variations in the intrinsic conscious organization should correspond, under fixed realization laws, to variations in the higher-level subject and its experiential unity, even when abstract equations remain unchanged. A viable theory must specify those counterfactual dependencies rather than merely naming consciousness as hardware. This test turns realization from metaphor into a structured explanatory commitment while respecting the empirical closure emphasized by physicalism.

novelty.explanation: This adds a new counterfactual criterion for constitutive causation that neither participant explicitly formulated.

thesis.text: The strongest physicalist position treats consciousness as a real higher-level property of organized physical systems, explained through validated multilevel identities, counterfactual mappings, and predictive integration without additional fundamental ontology.

novelty.explanation: This steelman strengthens emergence by adding identity and counterfactual requirements that answer the charge of merely labeling a higher level.

premises.text: Higher-level properties can be objectively real when they support stable explanation, intervention, prediction, and counterfactual dependence despite being multiply describable in lower-level physical language.

novelty.explanation: This develops the transcript's levels framework by stating criteria for higher-level reality and explanatory legitimacy.

premises.text: A complete consciousness explanation should map physical organization to experience, behavior, memory, report, and future dynamics while identifying which transformations preserve or alter phenomenal structure.

novelty.explanation: This extends the proposed perfect map with explicit transformation and phenomenal-structure conditions.

premises.text: Mary's new encounter with red can add acquaintance, recognitional abilities, and a new physically realized perspective without implying that her earlier propositional physical theory omitted a nonphysical fact.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the original response by distinguishing several kinds of epistemic novelty instead of citing only different neural activity.

premises.text: Established interaction constraints make additional behavior-changing conscious forces improbable at biological scales, while prediction-preserving intrinsic additions require an independent demonstration of explanatory advantage.

novelty.explanation: This combines the empirical and logical challenges without claiming that physics excludes every metaphysical reinterpretation.

premises.text: Private experience can enter science through structured reports, within-subject discrimination, neural covariance, and convergent behavioral evidence while retaining its distinctive first-person mode of access.

novelty.explanation: This gives the inclusive methodological reply concrete evidential mechanisms while preserving the epistemic distinction emphasized by the opponent.

conclusion.text: Physicalism is therefore warranted as a disciplined explanatory program when it develops testable multilevel identities and epistemic analyses; it need not claim that current mappings already settle every qualitative question.

novelty.explanation: The conclusion preserves the physicalist route while acknowledging that present mapping and relational description remain incomplete.

newArguments.title: Phenomenal topology program
newArguments.text: Instead of attempting to translate isolated qualities into particle vocabulary, physicalism can model the relational topology of experience: similarity, discrimination thresholds, compositional structure, attentional accessibility, temporal integration, and systematic behavioral consequences. It can then test whether transformations in neural-state space preserve the same structure. A robust structure-preserving mapping would explain why experiences differ and cluster as they do, even if primitive labels such as red cannot be defined nonrelationally. This program directly converts the shared limitation on verbalizing intrinsic redness into tractable comparative evidence.

novelty.explanation: This introduces a new empirical program based on structure-preserving mappings between phenomenal and neural spaces.

newArguments.title: Ontology surcharge principle
newArguments.text: When two theories preserve every physical prediction, the theory adding fundamental conscious properties assumes an explanatory surcharge. That surcharge is justified only if it yields independently specified composition laws, sharper modal constraints, or improved unification unavailable to the physicalist account. Merely naming an intrinsic basis does not yet pay the surcharge, but neither does prediction equivalence automatically refute the addition. This principle gives the unchanged-physics dilemma a proportionate comparative standard and avoids confusing empirical inertness with logical incoherence.

novelty.explanation: This adds a new burden-allocation principle for comparing empirically equivalent ontologies without dismissing metaphysical explanation categorically.
